title: Resolve four unreachable or inert runtime paths
description:
Four code paths are unreachable or inert in production. Each was surfaced while building the generated references in epic 004d10b7: binding a documented claim to the runtime that produces it exposed the path as having no live caller, no scheduler, or no reachable condition. None is a correctness bug today; each is a maintenance hazard, because a reader (or a projection) reasonably infers behavior the product does not have.

Resolve each by either wiring it up or removing it. Where a path is removed, sweep the prose and generated references that describe it in the same change (`@/inv/single-source-prose`).

## Findings

- `startup_recovery()` in `crates/jit/src/storage/claim_coordinator.rs` has no production caller. It is one of only two call sites of `TEMP_CLEANUP_THRESHOLD_SECS`; the other is `execute_recover` (`jit recover`), which is reachable.

- The auto-heartbeat interval is a configuration default with no production scheduler. `HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_SECS` is read as a config default (`agent_config.rs`, `config.rs`) and rendered into the runtime-defaults reference, but nothing schedules a beat; `jit claim heartbeat` records a single beat when invoked. A reader of the config key infers a background heartbeat that does not exist.

- The `exit(2)` warnings branch of `config validate` is unreachable. The handler carries the branch, but `result.warnings` is never populated, so 2 is never emitted. `docs/reference/exit-codes.md` documents the row as RESERVED for exactly this reason, and `crates/jit/tests/command_exit_code_projection_tests.rs` asserts that it stays documented as reserved. If the branch is removed, that row and its guard entry go with it.

- The cycle guard in `jit apply` is unreachable, and would report the wrong exit code if it were reached. `prevalidate_delta` calls `validate_delta_acyclic` (`crates/jit/src/commands/template.rs`), but a template delta cannot close a cycle by construction: `AnchorEdge` runs anchor -> node only, and a node's `depends_on` names other nodes only, so no edge ever points from a created node back to an existing issue. The guard's failure also maps to a bare `anyhow!`, so the classifier would yield exit 1, not the 4 that a validation failure implies. (The `apply`/4 row was removed from the exit-code reference in 3ac07340 for this reason.)

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Each of the four paths is resolved by wiring it into production or removing it, with the choice justified against the source.
- [hard] REQ-02: Every prose and generated-reference statement that describes a removed path is updated in the same change; no reference documents a path that no longer exists, and no reserved/exception row survives its cause.
- [hard] REQ-03: A path that is kept is exercised by a test that fails if its caller, scheduler, or reachable condition is removed again.
